text:
Philadelphia has spent November answering questions it would rather not hear: reports that Matvei Michkov is unhappy with his usage (Daniel Briere has told callers he isn't available), talk of the club opening the door to a Travis Konecny trade, and Konecny and Rick Tocchet both pushing back on talk of a divided room. Then the Flyers won three straight, the last on Noah Cates's goal with 31 seconds left in Montreal. Tonight Tocchet hands the net to Joseph Woll, who has been the steadier of his goalies: .892 in 13 games but 2.3 goals better than expected.

Our numbers are less impressed than the standings. The Flyers scored 14 goals on 7.7 expected in the streak, and for the season they take only 44% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets). The bright spots are young. Denver Barkey has eight points in ten games, and it's earned, much of it since a move to centre that has drawn praise. Owen Tippett is our depth sleeper at 21% to score after six high-danger shots in his last ten games. Trevor Zegras has gone four games without a point on 2.7 expected goals, which our numbers call due.

Washington is the mirror image, decent process and a miserable run. The Capitals are winless in five, outscored 30-16, and Saturday's 7-5 loss in Boston came with Elias Lindholm scoring four. For the season they're even on chances and -11 on goals, and goaltending (9.5 goals worse than expected) explains most of that. Logan Thompson starts after a short break; he was pulled against Buffalo after two goals in 25 seconds, and he's at -2.1 this year after +28.2 last year.

Alex Ovechkin, in what's been billed as his final season, has no goals in 16 games on 4.5 expected. Alex Tuch has goals in three straight and Ryan Leonard a five-game point streak. Jordan Kyrou is still out. Washington won the October meeting 5-2. The Capitals are 35% to make the playoffs, the Flyers 11%, and they sit four points apart in the Metropolitan.
headline: Woll in for a Flyers team winning loudly
